newsitem.title: BRAZIL: COFFEE - Brazil trees to blossom by mid-September.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE - Brazil trees to blossom by mid-September.

text.p: Brazilian coffee trees are expected to begin blossoming next week following strong rains that have put an end to the dry, winter period.
"Coffee trees will start flowering next week," said Jose Geraldo Rodrigues de Oliveira, superintendent at Cooxupe, a key Minas Gerais cooperative.
Coffee trees usually flower two to three times during this period, each time create new coffee berries.
However growers are not so optimistic about the amount of coffee berries that will be produced this year.
"We are expecting a normal blossoming no better than last year," said Critiano Otoni, a grower at Pocos de Caldas region.

They said leaves of many coffee trees have fallen due to fungus and a lack of rain at the beginning of the year. Fewer leaves means less protection from the sun, which could further damage the growth of coffee cherries into berries.
Although it is too early to estimate, growers feel the next crop will not be as good as the 1996/97 coffee crop.
"1997/1998 will not surpass the current crop," Otoni said, adding that coffee trees usually do not yield good crops in two consecutive years.
Estimates for the 1996/1997 crop ranges from 23 million to 27.5 million 60-kg coffee bags.
In the domestic market Escritorio Carvalhaes on September 4 quoted fine-to-extrafine Mogiana Minas green beans at 122/123 reais per 60 kg.
On the export market, Santos brokers Wolthers & Associates quoted specialty 17/18s at 15 over New York for October shippment, rising one point from last week.
Fine 17/18s was quoted at one under and Swedish qualities were quoted at nine under.
